etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French monarque, from Late Latin monarcha, from Ancient Greek μονάρχης (monárkhēs), variant of μόναρχος (mónarkhos, “sole ruler”), from μόνος (mónos, “only”) + ἀρχός (arkhós, “leader”), equivalent to mono- +‎ -arch.

definitions.definition: The ruler of an absolute monarchy or the head of state of a constitutional monarchy.

quote.citation: 1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Life of Henry the Fift”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene ii], page 25:
quote.text: Never was monarch better fear'd and lov'd / Than is your Majesty.

definitions.definition: A monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus) and others of genus Danaus, found primarily in North America.

quote.citation: 2019, Ocean Vuong, On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous, Jonathan Cape, page 223:
quote.text: But I know the monarchs are close by, their orange-and-black wings folded, dusted, and baked by heat, ready to flee south.

quote.citation: 1961, Nene Gare, The Fringe Dwellers, Text Classics, published 2012, page 41:
quote.text: ‘Skippy gets off. An ya know the first thing e says to them monarch? E turns round on em an yelps, “An now ya can just gimme back that bottle.”’

definitions.definition: (often capitalised) A stag which has sixteen or more points or tines on its antlers.
The chief or best thing of its kind.
Any bird of the family Monarchidae.
